'''Rowland Pettit''' (February 6, 1927 &ndash; December 10, 1981) was an Australian-born American [[chemist]].<ref name="ENC">[http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P004754b.htm Encyclopedia of Australian Science:Pettit, Rowland]</ref> He was awarded an overseas scholarship from the Royal Commission 1851 from 1952 - 1954. He came to London to Queen Mary College to conduct research into "the molecular orbital theory of organic chemistry and its application". 
<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/html/biomems/rpettit.html National Academies Press:Biographical Memoirs:Rowland Pettit; By John C. Gilbert]</ref><ref name="UT">[http://www.utexas.edu/faculty/council/2000-2001/memorials/SCANNED/pettit.pdf University of Texas:In Memoriam:Rowland Petti]</ref>
Pettit was noted for preparation of [[Cyclobutadieneiron tricarbonyl]] and the related [[trimethylenemethane]] complex.<ref name="ENC"/><ref name="UT"/><ref name="NAP"/>
Pettit was head of the Department of Chemistry<ref name="ENC"/><ref name="NAP"/> and W. T. Doherty Professor in Chemistry at the [[University of Texas, Austin]],<ref name="ENC"/><ref name="NAP"/>
a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="ENC"/><ref name="NAP"/><ref name="UT"/>
a member of the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref name="UT"/>
a member of the [[Chemical Society of London]],<ref name="UT"/>
a recipient of the American Chemical Society's the Southwest Regional Award,<ref name="UT"/><ref name="NAP"/><ref name="ENC"/>
a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="NAP"/><ref name="UT"/>

The [[University of Texas]] said that Pettit was an "internationally recognized organic chemist".<ref name="UT"/>

Early Career
[[File:Cyclobutadiene-iron-tricarbonyl-from-xtal-3D-balls.png|thumb|left|Cyclobutadieneiron tricarbonyl.<ref name="emerson">{{cite journal|title=Cyclobutadiene- and Benzocyclobutadiene-Iron Tricarbonyl Complexes|author=G. F. Emerson |author2=L. Watts |author3=R. Pettit |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.|year=1965|volume=87|issue=1 |pages=131–133|doi=10.1021/ja01079a032|bibcode=1965JAChS..87..131E }}</ref>]]

== Chronology ==
* 1927 born in [[Port Lincoln, Australia]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1949 B.Sc, [[University of Adelaide]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1950 M.Sc, [[University of Adelaide]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1953 PhD in chemistry, [[University of Adelaide]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1954 2nd PhD, [[Queen Mary College]] in London<ref name="UT"/>
* 1957 assistant professor, the [[University of Texas, Austin]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1960 associate professor, the [[University of Texas, Austin]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1963 professor of chemistry, the [[University of Texas, Austin]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1968 Southwest Regional Award, the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1970-1974 Chairman of Department of Chemistry, the [[University of Texas, Austin]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1973 elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1980 advanced to W. T. Doherty Professor in Chemistry, the [[University of Texas, Austin]]<ref name="UT"/>
* 1981 dies in [[Austin, Texas]]

==Scholarship==
Some of his work has been summarized with a focus on his synthesis of [[Cyclobutadieneiron tricarbonyl]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/om020946c |title=(Cyclobutadiene)iron TricarbonylA Case of Theory before Experiment |date=2003 |last1=Seyferth |first1=Dietmar |journal=Organometallics |volume=22 |issue=1 |pages=2–20 }}</ref>
